qs.q: Which of the listed scholars do the map and compass point to?
qs.why: The map and directions indicate geography and cartography, fields in which al-Idrisi was prominent.

qs.q: Decode the water, mechanisms and clock: which inventor does this combination represent?
qs.why: Al-Jazari was famous for inventing machines and water clocks, hence the water drop, gear and clock.

qs.q: Numbers and equations recall Al-Jabr wa al-Muqabalah; which mathematician is intended?
qs.why: Al-Khwarizmi wrote a book on algebra whose title helped spread the name of this science.

qs.q: Which Muslim physician wrote Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb, the medical encyclopedia in five books?
qs.why: Ibn Sina wrote Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb, which remained an influential medical reference for centuries.

qs.q: The eye, light and pinhole experiment point to the author of Kitab al-Manazir; who is he?
qs.why: Ibn al-Haytham studied light and vision and explained the pinhole chamber principle in his optical works.

qs.q: Which Muslim physician wrote a treatise distinguishing smallpox from measles?
qs.why: Al-Razi wrote a medical treatise describing smallpox and measles and distinguishing the two diseases.

qs.q: Which Muslim philosopher and scholar was associated with deciphering codes by letter frequency?
qs.why: The oldest known cryptanalysis treatise is attributed to al-Kindi and analyzes letter frequency.

qs.q: Which Muslim scholar studied India, wrote about it and was also known for astronomy?
qs.why: Al-Biruni accompanied journeys to India and wrote an extensive study of its culture and sciences.

qs.q: Which Muslim philosopher wrote Kitab al-Musiqa al-Kabir?
qs.why: Al-Farabi wrote an extensive book on music theory and philosophy.

qs.q: Which Andalusian philosopher explained Aristotle so extensively that Europe called him the Great Commentator?
qs.why: Ibn Rushd wrote many commentaries on Aristotle that strongly influenced Latin and Hebrew traditions.

qs.q: Which historian wrote Al-Muqaddimah within his Kitab al-Ibar project and studied human society?
qs.why: Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah introduces his historical book and analyzes society and history.

qs.q: Which Moroccan traveler recorded Al-Rihlah after travels lasting nearly thirty years?
qs.why: Ibn Battuta recorded his observations in Al-Rihlah after extensive travel in Asia, Africa and Europe.

qs.q: Which scholar and poet devised a geometric method for some cubic equations and helped reform the calendar?
qs.why: Khayyam combined mathematics, astronomy and poetry and helped reform the Jalali calendar.

qs.q: Which astronomer headed the famous Maragha observatory and wrote on mathematics and astronomy?
qs.why: Al-Tusi led the Maragha observatory, assembled astronomers there and wrote on astronomy and mathematics.

qs.q: Which Andalusian physician compiled Al-Tasrif and was famous for its book on surgery?
qs.why: Al-Tasrif comprised thirty medical treatises; al-Zahrawi's surgical contribution was especially prominent.

qs.q: Which physician described blood passing through the lungs between the two sides of the heart?
qs.why: Ibn al-Nafis described pulmonary circulation and rejected direct blood passage through the cardiac septum.

qs.q: Which Andalusian physician wrote Kitab al-Taysir on treatment and clinical observations?
qs.why: Ibn Zuhr's Al-Taysir combines therapeutic guidance with descriptions of clinical cases.

qs.q: Chocolate and a wristwatch indicate two industries famous in which country?
qs.why: Switzerland is internationally famous for chocolate and watchmaking.

qs.q: Which Andalusian scholar classified over a thousand medicinal and botanical substances in Al-Jami?
qs.why: Ibn al-Baytar's encyclopedia collected descriptions of plants, foods and medicines and their uses.

qs.q: Which Andalusian philosopher wrote Hayy ibn Yaqzan about knowledge on an island?
qs.why: Ibn Tufayl was famous for his philosophical Hayy ibn Yaqzan, which reached European readers in several translations.

qs.q: Which Abbasid writer was famous for Kitab al-Hayawan?
qs.why: Kitab al-Hayawan is among al-Jahiz's best-known works and presents information and accounts about animals.

qs.q: Which historian and geographer collected accounts of countries in Muruj al-Dhahab wa Maadin al-Jawhar?
qs.why: Al-Masudi combined history, geography and travel observations in Muruj al-Dhahab.

qs.q: Which historian wrote Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, covering events up to the tenth century?
qs.why: Al-Tabari's history is an extensive source of accounts from historical beginnings to his own age.

qs.q: Which Muslim scholar wrote Ihya Ulum al-Din in forty books?
qs.why: Al-Ihya is al-Ghazali's most famous work and addresses worship, ethics and conduct.

qs.q: Which poet's poems praising Sayf al-Dawlah al-Hamdani became famous?
qs.why: Al-Mutanabbi wrote his most famous panegyrics while at Sayf al-Dawlah's court in Aleppo.

qs.q: Which Persian poet wrote the Masnavi known as Masnavi-ye Manavi?
qs.why: The Masnavi is among Rumi's best-known poetic and intellectual works.

qs.q: Which Persian poet was known for five masnavis collected as Al-Khamsah?
qs.why: Nizami's poetic fame rests on five narrative poems collectively known as Al-Khamsah.

qs.q: Which Egyptian novelist won the literature Nobel Prize and was famous for the Cairo Trilogy?
qs.why: Mahfouz won the Nobel Prize in 1988; his works include novels about Cairo neighborhoods.

qs.q: Which Egyptian chemist won a Nobel Prize for tracking reactions on the femtosecond scale?
qs.why: Zewail developed methods for observing molecular transitions during reactions at femtosecond speed.

qs.q: Which Pakistani physicist helped develop the theory unifying electromagnetic and weak interactions?
qs.why: Abdus Salam shared the physics Nobel Prize for his contribution to electroweak theory.

qs.q: Which Olympic boxing champion announced his conversion to Islam and adopted the name Muhammad Ali?
qs.why: Muhammad Ali was a boxing champion and converted to Islam in the 1960s.

qs.q: Which American activist collaborated with Alex Haley on his autobiography?
qs.why: Malcolm X's autobiography appeared after his death; journalist Alex Haley helped prepare it.

qs.q: Which Mali Empire ruler's journey to Makkah with a gold caravan became famous?
qs.why: Mali reached its height under Mansa Musa, whose journey and wealth became widely known.

qs.q: Which leader established Ayyubid power and became famous for his wars in the Levant?
qs.why: Salah al-Din established Ayyubid political power and led their wars against the Crusaders.

qs.q: Which Ottoman sultan was called Al-Qanuni in Turkey for his legal reforms?
qs.why: Turkish sources called Sulayman Al-Qanuni because he collected and organized state laws.

qs.q: Which Ottoman sultan entered Constantinople in 1453 and was called Al-Fatih?
qs.why: Mehmed II entered Constantinople after a siege in 1453, and the city became Istanbul.

qs.q: Which Mughal emperor ruled India for nearly half a century and patronized art and architecture?
qs.why: Akbar ruled for about forty-nine years and patronized Mughal architecture and arts.

qs.q: Who was the fifth Abbasid caliph, ruling between 786 and 809?
qs.why: Harun al-Rashid was the fifth Abbasid caliph and ruled from 786 to 809.

qs.q: Which traveler recorded observations of Baghdad's embassy to the Bulgars on the Volga?
qs.why: Ibn Fadlan narrated a tenth-century Abbasid embassy's journey to the Bulgar ruler on the Volga.

qs.q: Which Andalusian writer recorded his Hajj (pilgrimage) from Al-Andalus to Makkah in Al-Rihlah?
qs.why: Ibn Jubayr's book describes his route from Al-Andalus to Makkah and the cities he passed.

qs.q: Which Mamluk historian wrote Al-Khitat on Egypt's topography and urban history?
qs.why: Al-Maqrizi wrote an encyclopedia of Egyptian history and topography known as Al-Khitat.

qs.q: Which Ottoman admiral wrote Kitab-i Bahriye and drew coastal maps?
qs.why: Piri Reis wrote a navigation book with nautical maps and coasts of the Old World.

qs.q: Which Ottoman architect designed the Suleymaniye complex and Selimiye mosque?
qs.why: Sinan was the Ottoman chief architect and designed Suleymaniye and Selimiye.

qs.q: Which musician moved from Baghdad to Cordoba and helped shape musical life in Al-Andalus?
qs.why: Ziryab moved to Cordoba during Abd al-Rahman II's reign and brought musical traditions there.

qs.q: Which Egyptian writer wrote Al-Ayyam and was known as the Dean of Arabic Literature?
qs.why: Al-Ayyam is Taha Hussein's best-known autobiography and a leading work of modern Arabic prose.

qs.q: Which Egyptian singer was called Kawkab al-Sharq?
qs.why: Umm Kulthum was among the Arab world's most famous singers and was known as Kawkab al-Sharq.

qs.q: Which astronomer wrote Jawami Ilm al-Nujum, which spread in Europe under the name Alfraganus?
qs.why: Al-Farghani's astronomical summary spread through Latin translations and was read in European universities for centuries.

qs.q: Which astronomer improved observations of the Sun, Moon and planets and prepared astronomical tables?
qs.why: Al-Battani was famous for accurate observations and tables used by later astronomers.

qs.q: Which Egyptian astronomer wrote Al-Zij al-Hakimi al-Kabir, containing tables and observations?
qs.why: Al-Zij al-Hakimi al-Kabir was a major astronomical work of Ibn Yunus, with observations and tables.

qs.q: Which mathematician and astronomer made accurate sine and tangent tables and studied trigonometry?
qs.why: Abu al-Wafa developed trigonometry and made accurate sine and tangent tables.

qs.q: Which mathematician separated algebraic operations from geometric representation and developed polynomial arithmetic?
qs.why: Al-Karaji treated algebra and terms arithmetically without relying on geometric representation.

qs.q: Which scholar designed Mizan al-Hikmah to study weights and density?
qs.why: Al-Khazini designed a precise balance and wrote on physics and mechanics in Mizan al-Hikmah.

qs.q: Which Andalusian author compiled Kitab al-Filahah on agriculture, gardening and animal husbandry?
qs.why: Ibn al-Awwam collected Andalusian agricultural knowledge in the extensive Kitab al-Filahah.

qs.q: Which Abbasid writer was known for works on language, literature and history?
qs.why: Ibn Qutaybah wrote on language, literature and history; his works include Uyun al-Akhbar.

qs.q: Which Andalusian writer wrote Tawq al-Hamamah on love and its states?
qs.why: Ibn Hazm wrote Tawq al-Hamamah in Al-Andalus, combining stories, prose and poetry about love.

qs.q: Which Egyptian scholar was among the most prolific authors of the Islamic heritage?
qs.why: Al-Suyuti was known for prolific writing on Quranic and hadith sciences, language and history.

qs.q: Which faqih (jurist) and hadith scholar wrote Riyad al-Salihin?
qs.why: Al-Nawawi wrote Riyad al-Salihin, collecting hadiths arranged in thematic chapters.

qs.q: Which Egyptian hadith scholar wrote Fath al-Bari, a commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari?
qs.why: Fath al-Bari is Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari.

qs.q: A city and a lamp combine in a familiar European nickname; which city is intended?
qs.why: Paris is known as the City of Light, combining the meanings of buildings and a lamp.

qs.q: Which traveling geographer wrote Ahsan al-Taqasim fi Marifat al-Aqalim?
qs.why: Al-Maqdisi recorded travel observations in an extensive geography of regions and cities.

qs.q: Trees and flowers suggest gardens and orchards; which Gulf city's name carries this meaning?
qs.why: The name Riyadh is linked to the gardens and orchards for which the area was once known.

qs.q: A new sign and a flower give an African capital's name in Amharic; which capital?
qs.why: Addis Ababa means new flower in Amharic, combining the sign and flower.

qs.q: Water ripples and earth color suggest a muddy confluence; which Asian capital's name means this?
qs.why: Kuala Lumpur means muddy confluence in Malay; its origins are linked to the Klang and Gombak rivers' meeting.

qs.q: Which ninth-century geographer wrote Kitab al-Buldan about cities of the Islamic state?
qs.why: Al-Yaqubi's Kitab al-Buldan presents cities, regions and administration in the Islamic state.

qs.q: Take the compass as north and buildings as a capital; which Chinese city's name combines them?
qs.why: Beijing's Chinese name combines north and capital, matching the direction and city in the puzzle.

qs.q: The sunrise direction and city image give the meaning of which Japanese city's name?
qs.why: Tokyo means eastern capital; sunrise suggests east and buildings suggest capital.

qs.q: The mosque suggests Islam and buildings suggest a city; which Asian capital's name matches?
qs.why: Islamabad means city of Islam, combining the mosque and city symbols.

qs.q: Which Persian historian and philosopher wrote Tajarib al-Umam and a book on refining ethics?
qs.why: Ibn Miskawayh was famous for his historical Tajarib al-Umam and works on philosophy and ethics.

qs.q: Breakfast and cafe pastries suggest a European country; which country shares this tradition?
qs.why: Baguettes and croissants are associated with bakery, breakfast and cafe culture in France.

qs.q: Mountains, deep coastal inlets and North Sea oil combine in which Scandinavian country?
qs.why: Norway is famous for mountainous fjord coasts and has an important North Sea offshore oil industry.

qs.q: A ball and trophy recall the first Arab hosting of the men's football World Cup in 2022; which country hosted it?
qs.why: Qatar hosted the men's World Cup in 2022, the first edition held in the Arab world.

qs.q: Which physician and historian compiled Uyun al-Anba fi Tabaqat al-Atibba?
qs.why: Ibn Abi Usaybiah collected physicians' biographies in Uyun al-Anba.

qs.q: Which historian from Al-Jazirah wrote the general history Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh?
qs.why: Ibn al-Athir's Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh covered the Islamic world's history up to his own age.

qs.q: Which geographer wrote the encyclopedic Mujam al-Buldan on cities and regions?
qs.why: Yaqut al-Hamawi collected place names and geographical and historical information in his dictionary.
